harbor_p05_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_001.text: By the seventh week, the smell of thawed mud had given way to tar warming on boat seams. Yue noticed the change before anyone mentioned the season. At the berth, a southbound vessel waited for room the Salt Lantern still occupied. Its passengers leaned on the rail and looked toward shore as though an occupied quay were a personal insult. The damaged ship had become a fixture in the town's arguments. Every delay could be measured in meals, lost work, or another vessel's inconvenient tide.

harbor_p05_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_002.text: Yan Su stood beside the revised handling plan with the south-berth keeper who had rejected the first anchor route. They checked the ordinary tackle positions again under morning light. The keeper, Yu Chao, pressed a stick into the partition's softened lower edge and found another small pocket of rot. Nobody called this proof the earlier inspector had lied. They recorded the new location, compared the old check note, and moved the planned load path farther from that face. The tubs would leave by a wider, slower route.

harbor_p05_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_003.text: Yue's inquiry shift began at the worker-property table. A carpenter named Peng Li had arrived to claim the tool roll Miao had questioned during the inventory. Peng brought a purchase receipt for the adze and a description of the handle repair. The roll remained inside the hold, so the commercial clerk could not yet compare its contents. Peng tapped his thumbnail against the dry table in irritation. Every day the tools stayed aboard meant another day borrowing an inferior adze from a man who made sure everyone heard about it.

harbor_p05_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_004.text: Miao produced no purchase term showing the merchant owned Peng's tools. He brought a ship hire sheet saying workers must supply their own hand tools unless otherwise agreed. The commercial clerk entered it as evidence supporting Peng's position rather than rejecting it because Miao supplied it. The agent looked surprised at the thanks. Yue understood the surprise. He had become accustomed to arriving as the person everyone expected to obstruct them. Producing an inconvenient page could feel like surrender before it became an accurate act.

harbor_p05_005.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p05_005.text: You can give us a source that weakens the claim you first made. We will preserve both the earlier claim and the source. The correction does not need a new story in which you always understood the tool roll correctly. Peng needs his tools, and the clerk needs a reason she can defend for releasing them. If your employer disagrees, he can identify the term he thinks we missed. Keeping the roll merely because he dislikes this page would be a different decision, without the same basis.

harbor_p05_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_006.text: Peng had expected an argument with Miao and disliked being deprived of it. He announced that merchants always tried to own the hands as well as the tools. Han Pei asked him to keep the discussion on his particular claim. He snapped that she had no idea what it cost to wait. Yue saw her begin to answer, then stop. She asked what paid work he had missed. Peng named two repairs. Han recorded the information for any properly submitted loss claim, without promising that the wage bond would pay for tools.

harbor_p05_007.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_007.text: Outside the shed, He Ming listened to Peng complain. She knew him from the yard and said his borrowed adze was actually sharper than his own. He denied it, then grinned. The quarrel he had brought into the office had found a friend who could tease it down to size. He Ming sent him to a boat builder who needed a simple brace fitted with ordinary tools. The introduction was personal, not an official employment guarantee. Peng went reluctantly enough to preserve his pride and quickly enough to show he needed the job.

harbor_p05_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_008.text: Yue helped place the table's clean forms under a weight before going to the dry alignment point. Yan Su had requested a single light-marker check, within the task she had already demonstrated. She inspected the marker and confirmed her reserve after rest. A brief extension guided it across the stationary reference line. Ordinary riggers read the result, then took the marker back. She withdrew her qi arms before fatigue, recorded the modest use, and returned to the table. The coming loaded haul relied on the keeper's approved rigging rather than her continued attention.

harbor_p05_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_009.text: The crew fitted the higher tackle while Sui Yan supervised the handling precautions. The tubs had been cleared for controlled movement, but residue on the lower surfaces still required protection and separation. An ordinary worker read each container mark aloud to the inventory clerk. Wen Zhi stood in the public viewing place with his old maker's drawing. Miao stood beside him, holding the merchant's invoices. Their rivalry had become a strange partnership of watching. Each feared the other's tub would disappear under a description nobody could challenge afterward.

harbor_p05_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_010.text: The first loaded movement went well. A tub rose from its resting cradle and cleared the damaged partition by the planned margin. The ordinary haulers moved together to Yan Su's count. At the dry shed, the receiving crew set it onto a prepared tray and secured it before unhooking. Sui checked the residue collection. The commercial clerk linked the inventory number to both claims. Bo shouted that one was done. Yan Su told him to save the celebration until the working lines were clear, then allowed a smile.

harbor_p05_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_011.text: On the second tub, the old partition moved although the load did not touch it. A crack opened above the rotted pocket, shedding pale crumbs onto the hold floor. Yu Chao called stop. Yan Su stopped the haul with the tub still supported by its rated line and cradle arrangement. Nobody remained beneath it. Sui ordered the visitor lane cleared while the keeper assessed the changed condition. Yue repeated the ordinary instruction at the shed door. Miao stepped back without complaint, his eyes fixed on the line.

harbor_p05_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_012.text: The sound came again, softer than the first break. It was harder to hear and more frightening because Yue could not tell where it ended. The keeper said the partition's unsupported upper panel might fall across the original exit route. The tub could not simply be drawn faster. Yan Su asked for the previously planned set-down position and got confirmation from both ordinary crews. They lowered it onto the clear support within the safe reach of the tackle. Only after it stood securely did the crew withdraw from the handling face.

harbor_p05_013.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_p05_013.text: We have a changed condition. The work stops while the keeper evaluates it. The southbound ship can wait, and its master can speak to the administrator about berth arrangements. He cannot buy us a sound partition by shouting from another deck. Yan, account for the crew at the dry point. Yu, identify what can be checked from outside before anyone goes nearer. Yue, keep this lane open for the carpenter. We will give the waiting owners a plain update when we have one worth giving.

harbor_p05_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_014.text: The southbound master arrived just as the captain finished. He asked whether the harbor intended to rot every ship before releasing one. Sui gave the stopped-work notice and the changed condition. He demanded a more senior official. She named the administrator's office and the lawful review route. Her jaw tightened after he left. Yue had seen her withstand pressure before, but not with a loaded tub set down beneath a broken wall. Duty offered a direction. It did not remove the captain's fear that she was failing everyone at once.

harbor_p05_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_015.text: The carpenter checked the panel from the approved higher position with a pole and a viewing mirror. He proposed external bracing after the loose upper piece had been isolated. Yu Chao rejected one brace face because it depended on the same softened timber. They argued quietly over the drawing rather than near the hold. Yan Su listened, then suggested transferring the load onto a temporary frame anchored to the sound quay structure, subject to its ordinary rating and inspection. The keeper went to examine that structure before accepting anything.

harbor_p05_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_016.text: Yue returned to the table while they worked. Han Pei had covered the forms with oilcloth. The page waiting beneath it carried Peng's description of the tool handle: ash wood, split near the end, bound twice with wire. The specificity steadied her more than the public quarrel did. Somebody had repaired that handle in a particular way because an object mattered to a day's work. The cargo problem was made of such ordinary things. It did not become less important because no grand secret lay inside them.

harbor_p05_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_017.text: He Ming arrived with a kettle and cups she owned herself. She set them outside the working boundary and offered tea to waiting claimants, charging nothing. Yue asked whether the packing lane had released her early. The woman said she had taken a free afternoon and intended to do something useful with it. She did not want a volunteer appointment. Han Pei thanked her, then warned her not to leave the hot kettle where the crew's lane turned. He Ming moved it before making a joke about the office's appetite for instructions.

harbor_p05_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_018.text: Wen Zhi accepted tea but would not sit beside Miao. The agent offered to hold his cup while he unfolded the maker's drawing. Wen looked suspicious, then handed it over. They spent ten minutes discussing the older tub workshop whose incised marks both knew. Miao's father had bought containers there years ago. Wen's brother had cut the marks. Their shared knowledge did not settle the invoice. It made the disputed objects seem less like prizes and more like things made by people who had once stood in the same dusty yard.

harbor_p05_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_019.text: The temporary-frame proposal returned with conditions. Port maintenance would supply its inspected ordinary lifting frame, rated lashings, and trained crew, all within the separately funded handling operation. The partition's loose piece would be restrained before the tub moved. A second clear set-down position had to remain available. Sui asked for the plan to include an abort point if the brace shifted. Yu Chao added one. Nobody reached into Yue's inquiry allowance or the wage bond. The people proposing the work had equipment and authority to account for it themselves.

harbor_p05_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_020.text: The crew did not restart that afternoon. The tide had narrowed their safe interval, and the captain would not trade a shortened check for the berth schedule. The southbound vessel received a temporary mooring assignment from the harbor master, with an ordinary shore boat for permitted passenger transfers. Its inconvenience remained real. So did the cost of risking the hold. Yue watched its first passengers land farther down the quay, disgruntled but safe. One complained that the town smelled of fish. He Ming said he had reached a harbor.

harbor_p05_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_021.text: At the repair shed, the keeper's son asked whether Yue had fought the broken ship. She described a stopped haul and a carpenter's drawing. He looked disappointed until she said the loose wall had made everybody argue about where to put a frame. He asked whether walls could argue. She said this one had made a persuasive noise. He laughed and drew teeth on a rectangle. The fish kite acquired a warehouse wall as its enemy. Yue did not correct the boy's mythology until he asked if the wall had been alive.

harbor_p05_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_022.text: Han Pei visited after supper with the office's public update, which she had been asked to read for clarity before posting. It named the paused cargo task and the next ordinary check, without suggesting that wages had been suspended again. Yue corrected one sentence that sounded as though every personal-property release had stopped. Already cleared collections could continue. Han made the change under her own signature. After the paper was put away, she asked whether Yue wanted to come to a boat-painting yard on her next free morning.

harbor_p05_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_023.text: The invitation pleased Yue because it required no useful answer. Han Pei knew a painter who allowed visitors to watch from the dry side. She had not visited in years. She said the yard would probably smell terrible. Yue said the repair shed's stairwell had prepared her. They laughed, then sat without speaking. Friendship had become comfortable enough to contain an evening in which neither woman improved the other. Outside, the port crew tested the temporary frame under ordinary conditions, and the dull hammer sounds traveled between the houses.

harbor_p05_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_024.text: The next morning's crew briefing began with the frame test results. Yan Su asked each worker to repeat the stop direction and their assigned route before entering the boundary. Bo rolled his eyes, then did it accurately. Deren watched from the seated stock station and corrected the count of spare slings. The foreman thanked him. A week earlier, Deren might have treated the thanks as pity. Now he knew exactly which sling had been overlooked and enjoyed the discomfort it caused a younger man who had hurried the list.

harbor_p05_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_025.text: Yue took the visitor relay post for the brief permitted interval before her inquiry work began. The ordinary clerk would relieve her at its end. She told Miao and Wen where to stand and what update they would receive. They both asked whether the tubs could be watched continuously. The captain approved a safe viewing position with no entry into the work line. Their right to observe would not become a right to touch. Yue repeated the arrangement once and left when the assigned clerk arrived, as agreed.

harbor_p05_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_026.text: The loose panel was restrained with ordinary bracing from the higher safe structure. The carpenter checked its fastening, Yu Chao inspected the frame, and the crew established the second set-down position. The work proceeded more slowly than yesterday's first successful haul. Nobody apologized for that pace. When the tub lifted, the brace held. A cracked edge dropped a small piece onto the empty hold floor. The keeper called a pause, checked the changed mark, and permitted the movement to finish only after the new condition was accounted for.

harbor_p05_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_027.text: The tub reached the receiving tray. Wen Zhi exhaled so loudly that Miao turned to look at him. The agent's expression held recognition rather than mockery. He had been holding his own breath. The commercial clerk recorded the successful move under the same two competing claims, making no title decision at the work face. The crew removed the hook after the tub was secure. Yue saw the ordinary slack return to the line and felt her stomach unclench. Her qi reserve had contributed nothing to the loaded task, which had needed better timber and planning.

harbor_p05_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_028.text: The remaining tubs came out through the revised route over two tide intervals. Several damaged sacks were isolated for disposal review after their contents failed the handling clearance. The captain's records identified samples and conditions rather than blaming the merchant for every loss. Wen wanted his loaned containers back cleaned. Miao wanted a tally of salvageable contents. Both could ask. The commercial clerk preserved their questions while the technical staff dealt with residue. Yue's property table received items the crew had previously been unable to reach.

harbor_p05_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_029.text: Peng's tool roll contained the repaired adze exactly as he described. It also held a small plane marked with another carpenter's initials. Peng said he had borrowed it and intended to return it before the voyage. The commercial clerk linked the new claim rather than pretending the whole roll had one owner. Peng looked annoyed at himself. He authorized the adze collection process and supplied the lender's contact point for the plane. One accurate description had recovered his property; another obligation still rested inside the same cloth.

harbor_p05_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_030.text: The plane's lender came the next morning, carrying a handle gauge that fitted a nick on the borrowed tool. Peng admitted he had meant to return it before sailing and then persuaded himself one more job would not matter. The lender wanted it back because his apprentice had been using a worn replacement. The commercial clerk arranged the supported collection after both confirmed the loan. Peng offered to sharpen the apprentice's blade as a personal apology. The man accepted without pretending a favor had erased the inconvenience.

harbor_p05_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_031.text: Afterward, Peng asked He Ming whether he sounded like a thief. She said he sounded like a man who wanted an uncomfortable act called something kinder. He looked wounded, then said she might try kindness once before the season ended. She laughed and offered him the kettle's last cup. Their old friendship allowed a bluntness the office could not use as a finding. Yue watched them share tea and thought about the different jobs a truthful sentence performed depending on who had earned the right to say it.

harbor_p05_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_032.text: Luo Jian's chest cleared the remaining handling review. The commercial clerk accepted his specific collection authorization after checking it through the recorded contact route. Fen came with the witnessed copy and her own identity evidence. She signed for the listed chest on her father's behalf, not for everything aboard bearing a similar sail stripe. Yue helped her carry it by ordinary handles with the tea seller's cart. The wood was heavier than the girl expected. She said her father had packed every useless thing he owned into the one object she had to fetch.

harbor_p05_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_033.text: At the tea stall, Luo opened the chest with his uninjured hand while Fen held the lid. The chipped cup survived. He said he kept it because it was the first one her mother had bought for their room. Fen had not known that. She had called it an ugly cup for years. He smiled and said it was ugly. The shared joke made room for the dead woman without turning her into the reason every present decision had to remain the same. Fen wrapped the cup carefully for washing.

harbor_p05_034.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_034.text: Inside the spare cuffs lay a little paper booklet of sums. Luo had practiced them to avoid being cheated on shifts. Fen recognized her own corrections in the margin. She had taught him when she was twelve, impatiently and with exaggerated sighs. He said the booklet had helped him check the camp wage. She touched the old marks and said she had forgotten being useful that young. Yue left before the conversation became private. Returning a chest had opened something no clerk could have inventoried in advance.

harbor_p05_035.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_035.text: Miao brought his employment term to the north office on the seventh week's middle afternoon. It promised a fixed fee for his voyage agency and a twenty-copper bonus only if the wage guarantee deposit returned untouched. Since five hundred forty-six copper had properly been drawn for unpaid wages, that condition could no longer be met. The document explained a financial pressure he had accepted. It did not establish that he hid addresses or falsified any receipt. Han Pei filed the term under his own supplied account.

harbor_p05_036.speaker: harbor_qin_shuo
harbor_p05_036.text: You were offered an incentive that rewarded the absence of a guarantee draw. The question is what you did under it. We already know one receipt was misclassified and corrected. We know you made a claim about tools that your later source did not support. Those acts can be examined on their own. The existence of the bonus does not make every mistake deliberate. Nor does calling it a normal commercial term prevent us asking whether it distorted the information sent to claimants.

harbor_p05_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_037.text: Miao said his employer would dismiss him if he spoke as though the bonus were improper. Qin said the harbor inquiry could examine its effect without deciding the whole employment relationship. The agent looked at the empty space on the page where a bonus amount would never be paid. Yue thought about the small pleasures her own eight copper had bought. Twenty could be a large hope in an ordinary person's account. It did not justify making someone else's earned wage appear unclaimed. It made the temptation less abstract.

harbor_p05_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_038.text: He Ming wanted to know why Miao had not disclosed the term at the beginning. He said nobody asked. She said people with an interest always waited for that excuse. Han Pei intervened before the room became a general argument about character. The inquiry would identify whether the required disclosure rule applied and what information he had supplied. He Ming left unsatisfied. On the lane, she told Yue that rules sometimes seemed designed to preserve a reasonable tone for people who had made others' lives unreasonable.

harbor_p05_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_039.text: Yue said tone could not be the condition for He Ming's claim to be heard. The woman stopped walking. She had expected a defense of careful wording, not agreement. Yue added that anger could name a real harm while still leaving intent to be proved. He Ming looked toward the office, then asked whether the two ideas could ever live comfortably together. Yue said probably not always. They went to buy cabbage for the evening meal. Choosing a firm head from the pile proved easier than deciding what to think of Miao.

harbor_p05_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_040.text: The boat-painting visit took place the following free morning. Han Pei wore an old coat because she refused to pretend she would stay clean. The painter was a broad woman named Duan who remembered her as a girl with more opinions than brush control. She handed Han a board and asked whether those proportions had changed. Yue watched the clerk blush, then pick a brush with deliberate dignity. On the test board, her first line wavered. Duan said good, now the day could begin without needing perfection defended.

harbor_p05_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_041.text: Yue tried painting a simple stripe and got a bead of color down the board's edge. Han laughed until her own brush shed a hair into the wet paint. They worked beside ordinary apprentices who ignored the visitors once the jokes ended. The yard paid its staff and owned its materials; their small practice boards were offered scraps, not equipment entrusted to them for harbor use. Han bought hers privately when Duan offered it for a coin. Yue declined to add a painted object to her already familiar pack.

harbor_p05_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_042.text: At lunch, Duan asked why Han had stayed at the wage desk so long. The clerk said the work needed doing. The painter answered that many kinds of work did. Han looked toward the boats rather than replying. Yue had used the same excuse in more places than she cared to count. Need could become a flattering way to avoid choosing. The conversation made the free morning uncomfortable in a useful way. Han left with her little board and no promise to abandon the office for a romantic new life.

harbor_p05_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_043.text: Back at the quay, Wen Zhi identified all six loaned tubs after safe movement. Four were empty or salvageable; two held spoiled material subject to disposal review. He did not get to pour the contents into the harbor simply because he owned the containers. Miao produced an employer's letter consenting to return the tubs if the supported contents claim and cleaning charges were addressed. The commercial clerk scheduled a hearing. Their agreement on identity had narrowed the dispute enough for a decision, but nobody had yet agreed who would pay the cleaning bill.

harbor_p05_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_044.text: For the hearing packet, the inventory clerk assigned the six loaned tubs stable identifiers T1 through T6. Their maker's marks remained in the descriptions. A cleared portion of contents from T4 received the separate lot reference R4. The distinction looked obvious on the full page: container title still disputed, contents condition cleared, claimed sale right awaiting its own supported release. On a narrow carrying slip, two columns sat close enough that the references nearly touched. Yue asked the clerk to leave more space when preparing the next copies.

harbor_p05_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_045.text: A hired porter read the narrow slip and asked whether R4 meant he could take tub T4 when its contents released. The commercial clerk said no and wrote the distinction onto his route note. He could move only the listed contents after an issued release, using an approved clean container supplied through the handling plan. The loaned tub stayed held. The porter looked irritated by another trip. Yue remembered his question because it showed how a correct full page could become a misleading object when only part of it traveled.

harbor_p05_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_046.text: Miao received the same written distinction for his employer's packet. He signed that he had received it, without conceding the remaining tub claim. The agent wanted cleared contents moved before storage charges increased. Wen Zhi wanted the containers returned without merchant paint left on their sides. Their urgency pointed in different directions. The commercial clerk set the hearing date and preserved the question. Sui Yan asked that any later move identify exactly what had cleared technically. Everyone left with enough information to act carefully, and enough frustration to act otherwise.

harbor_p05_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_047.text: Sui Yan asked the licensed handlers for separate estimates: safe disposal of spoiled contents, cleaning of containers, and continued storage. The estimates would go to the responsible account after authority and title were resolved. The captain would not announce a total that mixed all three as a single quarantine fee. The handlers were impatient because they wanted the job assigned. She understood that impatience and still required the split. Yue watched her revise the estimate request, then ask an assistant to bring food before the evening duty shift.

harbor_p05_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_048.text: A child from the southbound vessel wandered into the dry visitor lane looking for a dropped ribbon. She had mistaken the red quarantine tags for festival decorations. Yue called her back before she reached the marked boundary, then fetched the ordinary attendant responsible for passenger transfer. The girl's father apologized loudly, as though volume could finish the incident faster. Sui Yan asked for a safer waiting place rather than an apology repeated three times. The harbor master moved the family queue away from the active cargo gate that afternoon.

harbor_p05_049.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_049.text: The southbound vessel finally left its temporary mooring after an ordinary departure check. Its master sent the administrator a complaint about lost berth time and sent Sui Yan no personal thanks. The captain did not expect one. Yue watched the hull move into open water, its passengers already facing the horizon. A harbor held people's anger only while they were within reach. After departure, the records remained to explain what had happened. The people doing the explaining still had another tide's work waiting at their own feet.

harbor_p05_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_050.text: That evening, Deren brought Yan Su a handwritten suggestion for platform inspections. The letters were large and uneven because he disliked desk work. He wanted a removable cover, a visible check mark, and a second person to confirm hidden faces at the agreed interval. Yan said the cover existed now, but the confirmation shift needed scheduling. Deren replied that a thing not scheduled would be admired and forgotten. The foreman accepted the criticism. They took the proposal to the ordinary maintenance desk rather than calling it a permanent rule themselves.

harbor_p05_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_051.text: Bo listened to the older men and admitted he had once signed a check without lifting the cover because the lane was crowded. Yan Su asked when and where. The young rigger supplied the date. Deren started a furious lecture, then stopped when Bo said he was trying to make the record accurate. They reported the missed check through the named review route and inspected the affected fitting before reuse. The admission did not erase responsibility. It made an unexamined risk visible while there was still time to address it.

harbor_p05_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_052.text: Yue heard about the missed check from the public work update, not from reading Bo's private statement. She asked Yan whether he was pleased the boy spoke. The foreman said yes and angry that the event had occurred. Yue liked the refusal to choose one feeling. Their walk to the gate passed the temporary lifting frame, now cleaned and waiting for return to port maintenance. Its success had not made it the cargo shed's property. The keeper checked fittings and remaining loan items before signing the return.

harbor_p05_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_053.text: Han Pei's painted board appeared on the office window ledge the next morning. It carried a gull shaped more convincingly than her earlier drawing. A claimant asked whether it was an official seal. Han moved it to the private side of her shelf and explained that she had painted it on a free day. The man said she might do a better harbor emblem than the current one. She thanked him without promising to add another unpaid task. Yue watched her smile remain after the man returned to his wage question.

harbor_p05_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_054.text: The old loading supervisor's reply arrived from his new workplace. He remembered the household-address packet inside a canvas roll marked office, which was placed with shipboard bundles when two shore carts were exchanged at departure. He had believed it contained crew documents meant for the vessel. The instruction to deliver it to the north office had been folded inward. His account supplied a possible transfer error, not proof of what every person handling the roll knew. The keeper requested the cart tally and retained the original reply with its delivery reference.

harbor_p05_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_055.text: The tally matched two exchanged rolls but did not describe their contents. The former yard clerk's covering instruction matched the packet's internal address. No source yet showed Miao directing its movement. Han Pei wrote the supported chain and unresolved gap. He Ming read the public status with a grim expression. She could accept that a harmful failure might have come from several ordinary acts. It was harder to accept that such an explanation could still leave someone responsible without giving her one person toward whom every week's anger could travel.

harbor_p05_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_056.text: At supper, He Ming's mother asked why the town could not simply deliver papers in baskets that looked different. He Jun said it probably used whatever baskets were available. The older woman said then someone should make two different ties. He Ming laughed, but the idea stayed. Han Pei later proposed visible destination tags on office transfers, with a receipt at the receiving desk. The material would cost little; the assigned task and checking time mattered more. The proposal waited for the term review rather than becoming a miracle attributed to a clever mother.

harbor_p05_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_057.text: Yue took her seventh week's second paid inquiry shift to assemble the worker-property status pages. Most cleared belongings had been collected or had an authorized collection route. Peng's plane still needed its lender's confirmation. Two unclaimed bundles lacked descriptions from any claimant. Those objects would remain held under the commercial process with notice and a review date. She did not invent a person for them because the manuscript wanted its list completed. The harbor could preserve an honest unknown without treating it as permission to sell immediately.

harbor_p05_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_058.text: One of the unidentified bundles contained a child's shoe and a little brass clasp. Fen saw the inventory description on the permitted public notice and asked whether it belonged to a family that had left before winter. Yue directed the lead to the commercial clerk, who asked for a source and collection contact. Fen named the tea seller's former tenant. The clerk would send a safe-contact request, not publish the tenant's old private address. Fen smiled afterward. She had become a person who could supply a useful lead without promising to solve somebody else's absence.

harbor_p05_059.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_059.text: Luo Jian's fingers had begun to bend within the clinician's limited exercises. He still could not grip a loading strap safely. At the binder's shop, he had learned to sort paper by touch with his good hand and found the work less tedious than he expected. He complained about its lower pay and then defended the precision it required. Fen said he sounded like a clerk. He said she ought to know, having spent weeks correcting them. Their jokes had become less sharp as the ordinary shape of living together returned.

harbor_p05_060.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_060.text: Sui Yan's next handling notice cleared the empty spaces needed for a final hold inspection. The damaged partition remained isolated and would require a ship repair decision before any new voyage. Technical clearance of some cargo did not certify the vessel seaworthy. The captain directed the master to the relevant maritime inspection office. He argued that she was making his ship answer too many people. She said the ship had several different problems. Yue heard weariness beneath the reply and saw that she had learned to let an assistant take the next routine question.

harbor_p05_061.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_061.text: He Ming's mother visited the packing lane on the week's last free afternoon. She watched her daughter turn a heavy sack with a lever instead of lifting it in her arms. He Ming expected criticism and received a question about the lever's maker. The older woman said she had spent twenty years damaging her back because nobody showed her one. Their conversation moved from the tool to old work, then to the room rent. He Ming realized her mother had come to ask whether staying another month would burden her.

harbor_p05_062.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_062.text: They discussed the actual rent and food instead of performing two competing refusals to accept help. He Ming could afford the present month from her paid wage and current packing income. Another month would need a new choice. Her mother wanted to return to Willow Reach before the creek insects grew thick. He Jun offered to travel with her when his private arrangements allowed it. He Ming did not ask him to make a grand promise. She asked for the day he expected to know. It was a smaller bargain she could check.

harbor_p05_063.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_063.text: That night, Yue heard the family singing through the repair shed's open window. The tune had too many verses, and He Jun forgot the same line twice. He Ming supplied it angrily while her mother laughed. Yue had notes to finish but left them closed for a while. The sound carried none of the harbor's public success. It came from people who remained capable of annoying one another in the room their wages now paid for. When she finally wrote, the ordinary noise made the empty page less severe.

harbor_p05_064.speaker: narrator
harbor_p05_064.text: The week ended with the temporary frame returned, the revised walkway still under ordinary inspection, and the commercial hearing set for the following days. The wage bond remained at two hundred fourteen copper under its proper guarantee conditions. No tub title decision or cleaning payment had come from it. Yue had completed fourteen of her twenty-four inquiry half-days and earned twenty-eight of the forty-eight wage copper. Her own reserve had recovered after one light dry check. The harbor looked more open from the quay, although the claims behind its gates had become more exact.
